big_case.notes: The record concerns extensive border infrastructure, potentially irreversible environmental and historic-preservation injuries, and an important boundary between constitutional and statutory review. National policy consequences are substantial, though this is interim relief under a specialized statutory review scheme, not a final merits judgment.

leakage.notes: The log records forward work on October 23, before the November 9 disposition. Queries concern the originating district court, preexisting authorities, and other applications; the prose discusses underlying October orders rather than this application's result. All 105 results are unobserved, so null dates do not prove empty or pre-resolution returns. No query or reasoning affirmatively shows this application's disposing material; broad searches leave an audit limitation, not affirmative leakage evidence.

central_claims.basis: The November 9 docket and per-curiam writing grant a stay pending filing and disposition of the Government's certiorari petition, without immediately entering a merits judgment.
central_claims.claim: The Court will grant an unqualified stay of the preliminary injunction pending a timely certiorari petition rather than dispose of the case immediately through plenary review or summary reversal.

central_claims.basis: The docket records the Federation for American Immigration Reform amicus on October 29 and referral to the Court on November 9.
central_claims.claim: Justice Alito will refer the application to the full Court and at least one amicus brief will be filed before disposition.

central_claims.basis: The order issued November 9 after the October 29 response and October 30 reply. The document incorrectly gives the response deadline as October 28 rather than October 29.
central_claims.claim: The Court will most likely act between November 2 and November 9, 2026, after the response and reply.

central_claims.basis: The docket and complete staged per-curiam writing note only Justice Jackson as wishing to deny. The writings manifest contains only that per-curiam writing and no written dissent. This does not establish the unnoted Justices' private votes.
central_claims.claim: The stay will draw noted dissents from Sotomayor, Kagan, and Jackson, with a written dissent from at least one of them.

central_claims.basis: The staged per-curiam writing principally finds the major-questions claim statutory, applies the constitutional-claims-only review provision, and invokes Dalton.
central_claims.claim: If the Court explains the stay, its primary ground will be Section 102(c)(2)(A)'s preclusion of nonconstitutional statutory challenges, supported by Dalton's statutory-versus-constitutional distinction.
